**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Single tomato leaf, mostly green and intact
- Fine white/silvery stippling/speckling uniformly distributed across the entire upper leaf surface
- No discrete lesions, spots with borders, concentric rings, or powdery patches
- No yellowing, curling, or necrosis visible
- Leaf shape appears normal (not distorted or curled)

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Spider_Mites**: Fine stippling (pale dots from chlorophyll removal) across the leaf surface is the hallmark symptom. The test image shows exactly this — uniform fine white speckling with no lesions. Reference images confirm this appearance in early-to-moderate infestations.
- **Powdery_Mildew**: Would show distinct white powdery patches/coating, not fine uniform stippling. Eliminated.
- **Bacterial_Spot / Septoria / Early_Blight / Target_Spot**: All require discrete lesions with defined borders or concentric rings. None visible. Eliminated.
- **Mosaic viruses (Mosaic_Virus, Tomato_Mosaic_Virus, TYLCV)**: Would show mottled light/dark green patterning, leaf curl, or yellowing. Not present. Eliminated.
- **Late_Blight**: Large water-soaked blotches with white cottony sporulation. Eliminated.
- **Leaf_Mold**: Olive/brown patches on underside with yellow spots on top. Not matching.
- **Verticillium_Wilt**: V-shaped lesions, vascular streaking, wilting. Not present.

The uniform fine white stippling/speckling on an otherwise intact green leaf is the classic signature of spider mite feeding damage (sucking chlorophyll from individual cells).
